topics.label: Lecture opening and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the lecturer, the course context on cancer biology, and the main learning outcomes of the session.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, intrinsic versus extrinsic risk, and epidemiological patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the core nature of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease influenced by the microenvironment, intrinsic cellular errors, environmental exposures, public perception, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens as drivers of oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological agents such as viruses, bacteria, and parasites cause cancer, illustrated with the detailed mechanism and geographic distribution of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe specific exogenous carcinogens—including dietary aflatoxin, UV radiation, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, TCDD, and aromatic amines—and the biochemical pathways and xenobiotic metabolism through which they damage DNA.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and host developmental susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of tumorigenesis, focusing on the initiator-promoter paradigm, chronic inflammation induced by agents like asbestos, and the influence of host developmental stages on cancer risk.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the analytical and experimental methods used to determine carcinogenicity, including mutational signature profiling, human biobank epidemiology, animal toxicology studies, and the Ames in vitro test.
